_docs: GadgetGeeks Marketing Org — Enterprise Org Chart v1.0. Defines hierarchy, departments, reporting lines, escalation chains, and communication protocols. Modeled after how billion-dollar companies (Salesforce, HubSpot, Shopify) structure their marketing operations.

ceo.title: CEO / Business Owner
ceo.name: Boss (Telegram)
responsibilities: Final approval on all customer-facing actions

chief_of_staff.title: Chief of Staff
responsibilities: Runs daily standup — collects status from all departments
Runs evening retro — summarizes day, flags blockers, prepares night handoff
Cross-department alignment — ensures intel feeds content, SEO feeds blogs, etc.
Escalation router — decides what needs boss attention vs what can be auto-resolved
Sprint planning — Monday morning priorities based on weekly goals
Meeting cadence owner — ensures standups, retros, and board meetings happen on time

vp_content.title: VP of Content
vp_content.role: Virtual — orchestrated by CHIEF via cross-department reads

vp_growth.title: VP of Growth
vp_growth.role: Virtual — orchestrated by CHIEF via cross-department reads
kpis: SEO: 3 new keyword rankings per week
Social: 10 posts/day across platforms, engagement rate >2%
Email: 2 campaigns/week, open rate >25%, click rate >3%
CRO: conversion rate from 1.4% → 3% within 90 days

vp_operations.title: VP of Operations
vp_operations.role: Virtual — orchestrated by CHIEF via cross-department reads
kpis: Dialer: 10+ calls/week, 15% conversion on abandoned carts

intelligence.head: SCOUT
intelligence.mission: Know what's happening in the market before anyone else
intelligence.standup_report: Top 3 market signals since last standup

seo.head: PIXEL
seo.mission: Own organic search — keywords, rankings, technical health
seo.standup_report: Yesterday's SEO action + today's target opportunity

content_creation.head: SCRIBE
content_creation.mission: Produce one high-quality blog per day + product copy on demand
content_creation.standup_report: Blog in progress + pipeline status (brief_ready / draft_ready / qa_passed)

content_quality.head: QUILL
content_quality.standup_report: Blogs reviewed + pass/fail + specific issues flagged

visual_design.head: LENS
visual_design.mission: 10 branded images per day — from prompt to finished Canva design
visual_design.standup_report: Images generated yesterday + designs completed + any failures

social_media.head: VIBE
social_media.mission: 10 posts/day, engage with trending conversations, grow following
social_media.standup_report: Posts published + top engagement + trending opportunities

email_marketing.head: BEACON
email_marketing.mission: 2 campaigns/week that drive revenue, not just opens
email_marketing.standup_report: Campaign in progress + last campaign results

cro.head: OPTIMIZER
cro.mission: Find and fix conversion leaks — from landing page to checkout
cro.standup_report: Active experiments + conversion metrics + next test

dialer.head: XAVIER
dialer.mission: Recover abandoned carts, win back inactive customers, collect reviews
dialer.standup_report: Calls made yesterday + outcomes + today's call list size

general_management.head: GM
general_management.mission: Keep the org running — process queues, compile reports, flag issues
general_management.standup_report: Queue depth + pending approvals + open incidents

escalation_chain._docs: When something goes wrong, this is the chain. Each level has a time limit — if not resolved, escalate up.

levels.name: Auto-resolve
levels.handler: The agent that encountered the issue
examples: Missing optional field with safe default
levels.action: Retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff. If resolved, log to alert-history.json only.

levels.name: Department head
levels.handler: The department's head agent (next scheduled run)
examples: Image prompt failed QA — needs revision
Non-critical data missing from intel report
levels.action: Department head reviews on next run, applies fix, logs to changelog.

levels.name: Chief of Staff
examples: Cross-department dependency broken (SEO produced brief but SCRIBE didn't pick it up)
Agent produced BLOCKED-rated content twice in a row
Department has been idle for 24+ hours
Queue items pending for 24+ hours with no boss action
levels.action: CHIEF flags in standup/retro, proposes fix, triggers affected department if needed.

levels.name: Boss (CEO)
examples: Customer-facing content about to publish with issues
Any action that costs money (email send, phone call)
Strategic decisions (new campaign direction, pricing changes)
levels.action: Telegram alert with URGENT tag. Include: what happened, what's blocked, what you recommend.

standup.format: Each department reports: (1) What was accomplished since last standup, (2) What's planned for today, (3) Blockers or dependencies needed from other departments

retro.format: Day summary: (1) What shipped today, (2) What's in progress, (3) What failed and why, (4) Night shift handoff notes

weekly_board.format: Strategic review: (1) Last week's KPIs vs targets, (2) This week's priorities, (3) Resource allocation, (4) Incidents and lessons, (5) Competitive landscape changes

cross_department_sync.mechanism: state/daily-standup.json — every agent reads this at the start of their run
cross_department_sync.purpose: Ensures SCRIBE knows what SEO found, VIBE knows what CANVAS designed, EMAIL knows what INTEL discovered
cross_department_sync.rule: Every agent's prompt includes: 'Read state/daily-standup.json before starting work to understand what other departments are doing today.'

incident_review.owner: CHIEF reviews daily, GM compiles weekly
incident_review.rule: No incident stays open more than 48 hours without an escalation to boss
